problems.title: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
problems.notes: brute-force all 2^n subsets warm-up before you need backtracking with real pruning

problems.title: Subsets
problems.notes: iterative doubling (append each existing subset + new element) or backtracking — state both, iterative avoids recursion depth

problems.title: Subsets II
problems.notes: sort first, then skip adjacent duplicates at the same recursion depth to avoid duplicate subsets

problems.title: Permutations
problems.notes: backtracking with a 'used' set, or swap-in-place to avoid extra memory — the swap version is the sharper follow-up

problems.title: Permutations II
problems.notes: sort + skip duplicate branch: if nums[i]==nums[i-1] and !used[i-1], skip — the exact condition trips people up live

problems.title: Combinations
problems.notes: choose k of n; prune early when remaining candidates are fewer than what's still needed

problems.title: Combination Sum
problems.notes: unbounded reuse of each candidate — the recursive call keeps the same start index instead of advancing it

problems.title: Combination Sum II
problems.notes: each candidate used at most once, plus a duplicate skip at the same recursion depth — same trick as Subsets II

problems.title: Generate Parentheses
problems.notes: constrained backtracking: track open/close counts as the pruning rule instead of generating-then-filtering
